---
title: Posters and thumbnails
description: Show a still of each video in your pages, lists and link previews, with a token that can fetch only the poster.
---

Every encoded video has one poster: a JPEG of a frame near the start. Use it
as the player's poster, as a thumbnail in a list of videos, or as the image
of a link preview. For a private video, the poster can have its own token
that fetches the poster and nothing else, so a poster URL that leaks can't
play the video.

## Before you start

- A video that has finished encoding (`status: "ready"`). The poster is made
  with the first encode.
- For a private video, your app's signing key; see
  [Sign playback tokens](/docs/build/play/sign-tokens).

## What the poster is

- One frame, taken 1 second in, or halfway through a video shorter than
  2 seconds.
- A JPEG, scaled to at most 720 pixels on its short side, keeping the
  video's shape.
- One per video. There are no parameters for its size or its time, and no
  animated or storyboard thumbnails. To show a smaller image, scale it in
  your page or in your own image service.

A re-encode makes a new poster with the new output.

## Get the poster URL

```txt
Private: https://media.example.com/v/{token}/{playback_id}/poster.jpg
Public:  https://media.example.com/p/{playback_id}/poster.jpg
```

A private poster takes either a playback token (`aud: v`) or a poster-only
token (`aud: t`). A poster-only token is refused for anything else: the
playlists, segments, keys and subtitles answer `403 denied`.

### From a playback session

A playback session already carries a poster URL. `poster_url` from
`clipmux.playback.session()`, and from `clipmuxHandler`'s `/playback` route,
is signed with its own poster-only token that expires with the playback
token. `<clipmux-player session-url>` shows it unless you set `poster`.

### For a poster alone

On a list page you need the poster without a playback session. Sign a
poster-only token and build the URL:

<Tabs items={['Node', 'Python', 'Go', 'PHP']}>
<Tab value="Node">

```ts title="posters.ts"
import { ClipMux } from '@clipmux/node'

const clipmux = new ClipMux()
const { base_url } = await clipmux.app.get()

const token = await clipmux.playback.token('pid_…', { audience: 'poster', expiresIn: '1h' })
const { poster } = clipmux.playback.urls({ baseUrl: base_url, playbackId: 'pid_…', policy: 'signed' }, token)
// https://media.example.com/v/eyJ…/pid_…/poster.jpg
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">

With `playback_token` from [Sign playback tokens](/docs/build/play/sign-tokens):

```python
token = playback_token("pid_…", signing_key_pem, kid, audience="t", ttl=3600)
poster = f"{base_url}/v/{token}/pid_…/poster.jpg"
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Go">

With `PlaybackToken` from [Sign playback tokens](/docs/build/play/sign-tokens):

```go
token, err := PlaybackToken(key, kid, "pid_…", "", "t", time.Hour)
poster := baseURL + "/v/" + token + "/pid_…/poster.jpg"
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="PHP">

With `clipmux_playback_token` from [Sign playback tokens](/docs/build/play/sign-tokens):

```php
$token = clipmux_playback_token('pid_…', $signingKeyPem, $kid, null, 't', 3600);
$poster = "{$baseUrl}/v/{$token}/pid_…/poster.jpg";
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

Signing is local: a page of fifty thumbnails costs fifty signatures and no
calls to ClipMux. `app.get()` is cached, so the media origin is read once.

## Link previews

A poster-only token is safe in an `og:image` tag or a chat message: whoever
reads the page source gets a still, not the video.

```html
<meta property="og:image" content="https://media.example.com/v/eyJ…/pid_…/poster.jpg" />
```

Link preview crawlers may fetch the image long after you render the page,
so sign that token for longer, up to `max_token_lifetime_seconds` from
`GET /v1/app` (7 days by default). A public video's poster URL has no token
and never expires.

## Caching

The poster answers with `Cache-Control: max-age=300`, `private` for a signed
ID and `public` for a public one. Each token makes a different URL, so a
new token means a fresh fetch. If you show the same thumbnails on a busy
page, reuse a token for its lifetime rather than signing one per request.

## Check it works

```bash
curl -s -o poster.jpg -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}\n' \
  "https://media.example.com/v/$POSTER_TOKEN/pid_…/poster.jpg"
```

- `200 image/jpeg`: the poster is in `poster.jpg`.
- `401 token_expired`: sign a new token.
- `403 denied`: the token is for another playback ID, or signed with the
  wrong key. A poster-only token used for `master.m3u8` also gets this.
- `404`: the video isn't encoded yet, or the playback ID was revoked.
